parts.title: My first DIY disaster
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last spring, I decided to paint the bathroom myself. My brother had done it for his flat, and he said that it was easy. I bought blue paint, two brushes and a roll of tape, and I started on Saturday morning.

The first problem was the colour. In the shop, it looked like a pale sky, but on the walls, it was dark, almost black. The second problem was the ceiling. I was standing on a chair, and when I reached up, a big drop of paint fell on my head and went in my eye. I shouted so loudly that the neighbours knocked on the door.

At six in the evening, I finally finished. I stepped back to admire my work and put my foot straight into the paint tin. Blue footprints went all over the hall, through the kitchen and onto the sofa.

The next day, a friend who is a decorator came round. He laughed for five minutes, and then he repainted the room in white. Now I have a rule: I do the easy jobs, like changing a light bulb, and I pay experts for the rest.

parts.title: How to hang a picture
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Hanging a picture sounds simple, but many people make mistakes. [1] A few careful steps will save you a lot of time and trouble.

First, decide where you want the picture to go. [2] The centre should be at about the height of your eyes.

Next, mark the spot with a pencil. If you are not sure, hold the picture against the wall and ask a friend to tell you if it looks straight. [3] It is easier to rub out a pencil mark than to fill a hole in the wall.

Then, choose a nail or a screw that is strong enough. [4] Heavy mirrors need a special fixing that goes deep into the wall.

Finally, stand back and look at your work. [5] If it is not straight, a small tap on one corner usually puts it right.
sentences: Pictures look best when they hang in pairs.
A hammer is the only tool you will need.
Do this before you make any holes.
Old pictures can be worth a lot of money.
Think about the other furniture in the room.
Check whether the picture really is level.
Pictures are heavier than they look.
Most of these mistakes are easy to avoid.

gaps.explanation: "These mistakes" are the mistakes that many people make; the next sentence gives the careful steps that avoid them.
Think about the furniture when you decide where it goes; the next sentence says the centre should be at eye height.
Do this before you make any holes; the next sentence says a pencil mark is easier to rub out than a hole.
Pictures are heavier than they look, so the nail must be strong; the next sentence mentions heavy mirrors.
Check whether the picture is level; the next sentence says what to do if it is not straight.

parts.title: Changing a light bulb
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Changing a light bulb is one of the easiest jobs in the house, but it can still be dangerous if you are not careful. First, make sure the light is switched [1] and wait a few minutes. The bulb may be very hot. Then, take a chair or a small ladder, and ask someone to hold it [2] you climb. Turn the old bulb gently to the left until it comes out. Do not use too much force, [3] the glass might break. Put the new bulb in [4] turning it to the right, and stop when it feels firm. Make sure that the new bulb is the same size and type [5] the old one. Finally, switch on the light and check that it works. If [6] does not, call an electrician.

gaps.explanation: Switched off means the electricity is not flowing.
Hold the chair while you climb.
Or gives the warning: use no force, or the glass might break.
By turning it to the right: the way to do it.
The same as the old one: comparison.
It refers to the light bulb or the light.

parts.title: A message from a decorator
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: decorator
turns.text: Hello, this is Berit, the decorator. I’m calling about your living room. I came to look at it yesterday, and I have a few things to tell you before I start. First, the walls. They are in good condition, except for some cracks near the window. I thought they were next to the door, because that’s where the old picture was, but no, it’s the window, probably because the frame is very old. I’ll fill them before painting. The paint on the ceiling is also peeling, and I think it’s due to damp from the bathroom upstairs. The paint on the walls is fine. Please ask the owner of the flat upstairs to check the pipe. Now, the price. I said on the phone that it would be two hundred and fifty pounds, but that was without the ceiling. With everything, the whole job will cost about three hundred pounds. If you want a different colour on one wall, say a dark blue behind the sofa, it costs twenty pounds more, because I need extra paint and a second coat. How long will it take? I’d say three days: the first for the cracks, the second for the ceiling and the third for the walls. Not two, as I said before, because the paint needs time to dry. Please move the small things, like books and plants. I’ll cover the furniture with plastic sheets. I don’t use old newspapers, because they stick to the table. Finally, I’ll arrive at eight each morning and leave at four. Please call me if you have any questions, and I hope you enjoy the new room.

gaps.explanation: She thought they were next to the door, but they are near the window.
The walls are fine; the paint on the ceiling is peeling.

gaps.prompt: Altogether the work will cost around ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: Two hundred and fifty was the price without the ceiling; the whole job is about three hundred.

gaps.prompt: For one wall in another colour, add ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: A dark blue wall needs extra paint and a second coat, which costs twenty pounds more.
She said two before, but the paint needs time to dry, so it will take three days.

parts.title: An interview with a carpenter
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Eitan, you have been a carpenter for thirty years. What did you make when you were a boy?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: My grandfather had a workshop, and I spent every Saturday there. He made me a few wooden toys, as grandfathers do, but I started with small boats. I cut them from pieces of pine, and I sailed them in the bath. My mother wasn’t happy about the water on the floor.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Today you are famous for chairs. Why do you like making them?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: They aren’t quick, and they don’t make me rich, so it isn’t that. A chair has to carry a person for fifty years. It has to be strong, and it should be beautiful as well. Making something that is both is very difficult, and that’s why I love it.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How long does a chair take?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Not two days, that’s what customers hope. Two months would be a big table with carvings. A good chair takes me about two weeks, if I work every day. The wood needs time to dry and the glue needs time to set, and you can’t hurry that.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Tell me about your biggest mistake.

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Oh, I can laugh about it now. A chair that broke would be a small embarrassment, and I once built a table with three legs, because I forgot one. But the worst was a beautiful bed for a customer. Nothing was wrong with it, except that it was too big for the door. We had to take out a window to get it in.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What advice do you give to beginners?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Don’t buy new machines. They are expensive and you don’t need them at the beginning. And don’t be in a hurry. The most important thing is to keep your tools sharp. A sharp tool is safer, because you don’t need to push so hard, and the cut is cleaner.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: You still use hand tools. Why?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Machines are faster, and they make a lot of dust, but the hand tools aren’t really cheaper. For me, it’s about learning. When you use a plane, you feel the wood: the way it wants to go and where it is hard. A machine hides all of that from you. I think a carpenter who doesn’t know the wood is only an operator.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Thank you very much, Eitan.
